triage.note: The half of D11 the cost argument lives on, and the one a refactor is most likely to break silently. A modern full-taxonomy real filing extracts cleanly, so the D8 document-level signal stays quiet, so the router must return before it reaches a tier: no call, no dollar, and — asserted by `escalation_invariant`, which re-runs the same file with the flag off — an envelope identical in every field determinism governs, differing only by the `routing` key itself. `cat-2023` is deliberately the same fixture ADR-035 section e2 made the eval set's exact-`success` pin, so if the escalation path ever emits a warning on a clean filing this case reports it twice over. The three `item_field` pins carry the item-level half: with the trigger quiet, no item may claim an escalation `method`.
triage.note_negative_space: This case cannot show that a tier WORKS — nothing here ever calls one. It shows that a clean filing costs nothing, which is a different and much cheaper claim.

provenance: D11, created 2026-08-26 before src/sec10k/escalate.py existed, per hard rule 2. Red at origin/main (5a44758), measured rather than assumed — record in tasks/reviews/d11-red-first.txt. TWO failures, not the whole case, and the reason is worth stating because it is the shape a reviewer should be suspicious of: origin/main's sec10k adapter never passes `escalate` at all, so the extra input key is silently ignored and every check that does not name routing still passes over a perfectly good deterministic run. The two that go red are `routing` (unknown check type 'routing') and `escalation_invariant` (the same). The case is red-first on exactly the claims it adds, and on nothing else.
